questions.q: Why was all of Israel willing to anoint David as king over Israel?
questions.a: David was a member of the same nation as they were, he had led Israel’s army in the past, and Yahweh had told Samuel that David would become king over Israel.

questions.q: How did Joab become the commander of David’s army?
questions.a: David said that whoever led the attack against the Jebusites first would become commander, and Joab attacked first, so he became commander.

questions.q: Why did David become greater and greater after he began to live in the city of David?
questions.a: David became greater and greater because Yahweh of Armies was with him.

questions.q: What did David’s greatest warriors help him become?
questions.a: They helped make him a strong and secure king over Israel, just as Yahweh had said would happen.
Jashobeam killed three hundred men with his spear on one occasion.

questions.q: What was Eleazar the Ahohite known for?
questions.a: After the Israelite army had fled, Eleazar the Ahohite stood with David in the middle of the barley field and cut down the Philistines.

questions.q: Where was David staying when three of his mighty warriors came to him?
questions.a: David was staying in the stronghold at the cave of Adullam, while a group of Philistine soldiers occupied Bethlehem.

questions.q: What was the request which David made?
questions.a: David wanted some water to drink from the well near the gate at Bethlehem.

questions.q: What did the three mighty men of David do to make his request a reality?
questions.a: The three mighty men of David broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David.

questions.q: Why did David not drink the water from the well in Bethlehem when his mighty men had risked their lives to get it?
questions.a: David refused to drink the water because doing so would be like drinking the blood of the men who had risked their lives to get it for him.

questions.q: Who was Abishai, brother of Joab, and why was he famous?
questions.a: Abishai was the leader of the next three of David’s greatest soldiers, and he had once killed three hundred enemy soldiers with his spear.

questions.q: What was the reputation of Benaiah, son of Jehoiada?
questions.a: Benaiah was a strong man who killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day, and he killed a large Egyptian soldier by taking the Egyptian’s own spear and killing him with it.

questions.q: What responsibility did David give to Benaiah?
questions.a: Benaiah was highly regarded by David, so he put him in charge of his bodyguard.

questions.q: Which of the mighty men was the brother of Joab?
questions.a: Asahel was the mighty man who was the brother of Joab.

questions.q: Whose armor-bearer was Naharai the Beerothite?
questions.a: Naharai the Beerothite carried the weapons of Joab, the son of Zeruiah.

questions.q: What made Adina notable among David’s warriors?
questions.a: Adina was a leader of the tribe of Reuben, and thirty men served with him.

commentary.text: A list of David's mighty men.

Verses 1–9 David was brought to possess the throne of Israel after he had reigned seven years in Hebron, over Judah only. God's counsels will be fulfilled at last, whatever difficulties lie in the way. The way to be truly great, is to be really useful, to devote all our talents to the Lord.

An account is given of David's worthies, the great men who served him. Yet David reckoned his success, not as from the mighty men that were with him, but from the mighty God, whose presence is all in all. In strengthening him, they strengthened themselves and their own interest, for his advancement was theirs. We shall gain by what we do in our places for the support of the kingdom of the Son of David; and those that are faithful to Him, shall find their names registered much more to their honour, than these are in the records of fame.
